news.title: Paysafe’s Wallet Growth Meets Slower Payments And A Debt-Heavy Balance Sheet
news.body: Paysafe reported a third-quarter payments slowdown alongside growth in digital wallets. The company disclosed $2.5 billion of debt and $250.7 million of cash at September 30 following refinancing, making the earnings contribution from that wallet growth particularly important. The next test is whether enterprise-merchant activation and wallet revenue per user improve—not simply whether wallet activity rises.

news.title: Chase Blocks Shared-Card AI Purchases As Virtual Workarounds Add Merchant Costs
news.body: JPMorgan Chase is blocking AI-agent purchases made with card numbers customers give agents, according to Wall Street Journal reporting relayed by PYMNTS. Stripe’s Link can instead issue single-use virtual cards, but merchants reported higher acceptance costs from commercial-card classification and difficulties processing returns. Merchants evaluating agent checkout must distinguish issuer-supported agentic tokens from virtual-card fallbacks and test acceptance costs and refund matching separately.

source.name: PYMNTS, reporting on The Wall Street Journal

news.title: Griffin Raises $20 Million For Planned Card And Stablecoin Expansion
news.body: Griffin raised $20 million and outlined plans to expand into cards and stablecoins. The financing supports a broader product ambition, but planned services do not yet give fintech customers additional live payment capabilities. Prospective customers should tie integration decisions to actual card availability, processing arrangements and permissions for stablecoin reserve services.

news.title: Microsoft’s Second-Day Recovery Puts Backup Communications Workflows On The Payments Checklist
news.body: Microsoft said it had addressed the technical cause of a disruption affecting services including Outlook, Teams and Copilot across more than 70 countries, while restoration continued for remaining customers and regions. For banks, payment companies and merchants, the documented exposure concerns communications and operating workflows—not a reported clearing or settlement outage. Payments teams should test approved backup channels for payment approvals, customer support and fraud callbacks, then compare their dependencies with Microsoft’s promised post-incident report.

news.title: Thailand’s Proposed Stablecoin Limits Distinguish Own-Account Transfers From Third-Party Payments
news.body: Thailand has proposed rules that would cap certain stablecoin transfers at approximately $148,000 daily and permit transfers only between accounts or wallets belonging to the same person, The Block reported. Within the proposal’s scope, that same-owner condition would separate moving a customer’s own funds from paying another person or business. Thai digital-asset platforms should map those two transaction types separately and establish covered assets, exemptions and implementation dates before changing customer access.

perspective: Chase’s AI purchase blocks and Thailand’s proposed stablecoin limits put payment permissions alongside funding and service reliability on today’s agenda.

curiosity.text: In 1987, the U.S. Federal Reserve began requiring banks to use nine-digit routing numbers in electronic payments, adding a check digit that helps detect mistyped numbers. The final digit is calculated from the preceding eight using a weighted formula, so it can catch many—but not all—keying errors. Source: Federal Reserve Financial Services, “Routing Number Policy” — https://www.frbservices.org/resources/routing-number-policy
